punchline: On a quiz show, strangers in the studio beat the friends chosen for being clever.
thirty_sec: On Who Wants to Be a Millionaire?, Surowiecki reports, phoned-in experts were right about 65 percent of the time and the studio audience about 91 percent. Not a controlled study, but the gap was wide: many partial minds beat one deep one.
question: Which question on your desk would a mixed group answer better than your usual expert?
key_contrast: One deep mind, or many scattered ones.
